newsitem.title: UK: UK businessmen urge progress on EU single market.
newsitem.headline: UK businessmen urge progress on EU single market.

text.p: A report by leading British businessmen concludes Europe's companies lag badly behind U.S. and Japanese rivals in competitiveness due partly to inertia in Brussels and a preoccupation with European monetary union, the Financial Times said on Monday.
The newspaper said the group, headed by Lord Sheppard, would call on business to work for radical change in Brussels and for greater emphasis on completion of the European single market.

Lord Sheppard, former chairman of food and leisure company Grand Metropolitan, told the Financial Times in an interview that progress towards a single market had stalled because of the focus on monetary union.
"We need to recapture the excitement that surrounded the 1992 initiative and give the single market the same priority as the single currency which is less important for business," he said.

The Financial Times said the report, due to be published after Britain's May 1 general election, was drawn up by a working party of 19 senior business figures including British Petroleum chairman Sir David Simon.
